points.title: 早年成长与文学创作
points.description: 本杰明·迪斯雷利出生于伦敦的一个犹太裔家庭，父亲是文学评论家。他接受了良好的教育，但15岁时因与父亲发生争执被逐出学校。随后他自学法律，但最终转向文学创作。1826年，他发表了第一部小说《维维安·格雷》，获得了成功。这一时期，他积极参与社交圈，结识了许多重要人物，同时也开始关注政治。他的文学作品展现了对社会问题的关注，并逐渐形成了自己独特的政治观点。伦敦的这段经历为他后来的政治生涯奠定了基础，培养了他的雄辩才能和社交技巧。
points.descriptionEn: Benjamin Disraeli was born in London to a Jewish family; his father was a literary critic. He received a good education but was expelled from school at 15 after a quarrel with his father. He then studied law independently but eventually turned to literature. In 1826, he published his first novel, 'Vivian Grey,' which was a success. During this period, he actively participated in social circles, met important people, and began to develop an interest in politics. His literary works showed concern for social issues and gradually formed his unique political views. This London experience laid the foundation for his later political career, developing his oratorical skills and social abilities.

points.title: 初入政坛
points.description: 1837年，迪斯雷利当选为下议院议员，正式进入政坛。他最初以独立保守派身份活跃，很快展现出非凡的政治才能。他支持《1832年改革法案》，但反对进一步的激进改革。在议会中，他以雄辩的演说风格和机智的辩论技巧著称，逐渐成为保守党内的年轻领袖。这一时期，他与保守党领袖罗伯特·皮尔关系复杂，既有合作也有分歧。迪斯雷利开始关注工人阶级问题，提出了一些改善工人状况的温和改革建议，这为他后来成为'托利民主'的倡导者奠定了基础。伦敦的议会生涯使他积累了丰富的政治经验，并建立了广泛的人脉关系。
points.descriptionEn: In 1837, Disraeli was elected to the House of Commons, officially entering politics. Initially active as an independent Conservative, he quickly demonstrated remarkable political talent. He supported the Reform Act of 1832 but opposed further radical reforms. In Parliament, he became known for his eloquent speaking style and witty debating skills, gradually emerging as a young leader within the Conservative Party. During this period, his relationship with Conservative leader Robert Peel was complex, involving both cooperation and disagreement. Disraeli began to focus on working-class issues, proposing moderate reform suggestions to improve workers' conditions, laying the foundation for his later advocacy of 'Tory Democracy.' His parliamentary career in London provided him with extensive political experience and established broad connections.

points.title: 保守党改革与领袖崛起
points.titleEn: Conservative Party Reform and Rise to Leadership
points.description: 1845年后，迪斯雷利在保守党内的影响力日益增强。他批评皮尔的自由贸易政策，并在1845-1846年的谷物法争议中与皮尔决裂。这一时期，他致力于重塑保守党，使其能够适应工业社会的新挑战。他提出了'托利民主'理念，试图将保守主义与民主制度相结合，扩大保守党的社会基础。1852年、1858年和1859年，他短暂担任财政大臣，展现出经济管理才能。1866年，当保守党重新掌权时，迪斯雷利成为下议院领袖。这一阶段，他逐渐从边缘人物成长为保守党的核心领导人，为后来的首相生涯奠定了基础。伦敦的政治舞台成为他施展才华的主要场所，他的政治理念也在此期间逐渐成熟。
points.descriptionEn: After 1845, Disraeli's influence within the Conservative Party grew. He criticized Peel's free trade policies and broke with him during the Corn Law controversy of 1845-1846. During this period, he worked to reshape the Conservative Party to adapt to the new challenges of industrial society. He proposed the concept of 'Tory Democracy,' attempting to combine conservatism with democratic institutions and expand the social base of the Conservative Party. He served briefly as Chancellor of the Exchequer in 1852, 1858, and 1859, demonstrating economic management skills. In 1866, when the Conservatives returned to power, Disraeli became Leader of the House of Commons. During this phase, he gradually grew from a marginal figure to a central leader of the Conservative Party, laying the foundation for his later premiership. London's political stage became the main venue for him to display his talents, and his political ideas gradually matured during this period.

points.title: 首相任期
points.description: 1868年，迪斯雷利首次担任英国首相，尽管任期短暂仅到同年12月，但已展现其领导风格。1874年，他再次出任首相，并连续执政直到1880年，这是他政治生涯的巅峰时期。作为首相，他推动了一系列重要改革，包括《公共卫生法》、《艺术鼓励法》等，改善了城市工人阶级的生活条件。在外交方面，他奉行'光荣孤立'政策，1875-1878年通过外交手段获得苏伊士运河控制权，1878年柏林会议上提升了英国的国际地位。1876年，他授予维多利亚女王'印度女皇'称号，巩固了大英帝国的统一。这一时期，他与自由党领袖威廉·格拉德斯通展开激烈的政治竞争，两人的辩论成为英国政治史上的经典。伦敦作为政治中心，见证了迪斯雷利作为首相的各项决策及其对英国历史的影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1868, Disraeli became Prime Minister of the UK for the first time, though his tenure was brief, ending in December of the same year, yet it already showcased his leadership style. In 1874, he returned as Prime Minister and served continuously until 1880, the peak of his political career. As Prime Minister, he pushed through a series of important reforms, including the Public Health Act and the Art Encouragement Act, improving living conditions for the urban working class. In foreign policy, he pursued a 'splendid isolation' policy, gaining control of the Suez Canal through diplomatic means in 1875-1876, and enhancing Britain's international standing at the Berlin Conference in 1878. In 1876, he granted Queen Victoria the title 'Empress of India,' consolidating the unity of the British Empire. During this period, he engaged in fierce political competition with Liberal leader William Gladstone, with their debates becoming classics in British political history. London, as the political center, witnessed Disraeli's decisions as Prime Minister and their impact on British history.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 1880年大选失败后，迪斯雷利成为下议院反对党领袖，但健康状况已开始恶化。1881年4月，他因严重疾病辞去党领袖职务，同年4月19日在伦敦的家中去世，享年76岁。临终前，维多利亚女王亲临探望，并授予他比尔特伯爵头衔，使他成为第一位获此荣誉的犹太裔英国人。迪斯雷利去世后，被安葬在伦敦的休恩登圣米迦勒教堂。他的政治遗产深远，他重塑了保守党，使其成为能够适应民主时代的政党；他推行的社会改革改善了工人阶级生活；他的外交政策扩大了英国影响力。此外，他的文学作品和演讲风格也影响了英国政治文化。伦敦作为他一生的主要活动场所，见证了他从文学青年到政治领袖的转变，以及他留给英国的政治和文化遗产。
points.descriptionEn: After losing the 1880 general election, Disraeli became Leader of the Opposition in the House of Commons, but his health had begun to deteriorate. In April 1881, due to serious illness, he resigned as party leader and died at his home in London on April 19, at the age of 76. Shortly before his death, Queen Victoria visited him personally and granted him the title Earl of Beaconsfield, making him the first Jewish-born Briton to receive this honor. After his death, Disraeli was buried at St Michael's Church, Hughenden, London. His political legacy is profound: he reshaped the Conservative Party into one capable of adapting to the democratic era; the social reforms he implemented improved working-class living conditions; his foreign policy expanded British influence. Additionally, his literary works and oratorical style influenced British political culture. London, as the main venue for his activities throughout his life, witnessed his transformation from a literary youth to a political leader and the political and cultural legacy he left to Britain.

appraisal.zh: 迪斯雷利通常被视为英国保守党转型的关键人物，他以「托利民主」扩大党的社会基础，任内推动社会改革、改善工人生活，又借外交取得苏伊士运河控制权并在柏林会议上提升英国影响，还与维多利亚女王关系密切。不过也有研究者指出，他立场多变、被视为机会主义者，改革不够彻底，外交上的「光荣孤立」失于短视，与格拉德斯通的竞争过于个人化。总体而言，他被看作一位务实而具远见的政治家，其遗产深刻影响英国保守主义。
appraisal.en: Disraeli is generally seen as a key figure in the Conservative Party's transformation: his 'Tory Democracy' broadened its social base, his domestic reforms improved working-class conditions, his foreign policy secured the Suez Canal and raised British influence at the Berlin Conference, and he cultivated a close bond with Queen Victoria. Yet some researchers note his shifting positions and opportunism, reforms judged insufficient, a short-sighted 'splendid isolation', and an overly personal rivalry with Gladstone. On balance he is regarded as a pragmatic, far-sighted statesman whose legacy shaped British conservatism.

supporter.zh: 迪斯雷利被视为英国历史上最伟大的保守党领袖之一。他成功地将保守党从贵族党转变为能够适应民主时代的现代政党，提出了'托利民主'理念，扩大了党的社会基础。作为首相，他推动了多项社会改革，改善了工人阶级的生活条件，同时维护了英国的大国地位。他的外交政策使英国获得了苏伊士运河控制权，并在柏林会议上提升了国际影响力。迪斯雷利还与维多利亚女王建立了密切关系，强化了君主立宪制。他的雄辩才能和政治智慧使他成为英国政治史上的传奇人物。
supporter.en: Disraeli is regarded as one of the greatest Conservative leaders in British history. He successfully transformed the Conservative Party from an aristocratic party into a modern party capable of adapting to the democratic era, proposing the concept of 'Tory Democracy' and expanding the party's social base. As Prime Minister, he pushed through numerous social reforms that improved living conditions for the working class while maintaining Britain's great power status. His foreign policy gained Britain control of the Suez Canal and enhanced its international influence at the Berlin Conference. Disraeli also established a close relationship with Queen Victoria, strengthening the constitutional monarchy. His oratorical talent and political wisdom made him a legendary figure in British political history.

critic.zh: 批评者认为迪斯雷利的政治生涯存在诸多争议。他被指责为机会主义者，政治立场常常摇摆不定，尤其是在宗教问题上从犹太教改宗基督教以适应政治环境。他的社会改革虽然改善了工人阶级生活，但被批评为不够彻底，未能从根本上解决社会不平等问题。在外交政策上，他推行的'光荣孤立'政策被批评为短视，未能有效应对欧洲列强崛起的挑战。此外，他与格拉德斯通的激烈政治竞争被批评为过于个人化，损害了英国政治的理性讨论氛围。批评者还指出，他虽然扩大了选举权，但本质上仍维护精英统治。
critic.en: Critics argue that Disraeli's political career was marked by numerous controversies. He is accused of being an opportunist with frequently shifting political positions, particularly in religious matters, converting from Judaism to Christianity to adapt to the political environment. Although his social reforms improved working-class conditions, they are criticized as insufficient and failing to fundamentally address social inequality. His 'splendid isolation' foreign policy is criticized as short-sighted, unable to effectively address the challenges posed by rising European powers. Additionally, his fierce political competition with Gladstone is criticized as overly personal, damaging the atmosphere of rational political discourse in Britain. Critics also note that while he expanded suffrage, he fundamentally maintained elite rule.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，迪斯雷利被视为英国政治转型期的关键人物。他代表了19世纪英国从贵族政治向民主政治过渡的复杂过程。历史学家普遍认为他是一位务实的政治家，能够平衡传统与变革。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为雄辩家和政治策略大师，与格拉德斯通的竞争被视为英国政治史上的经典对决。他的文学作品和政治著作也受到研究，被视为理解19世纪英国政治思想的重要资料。迪斯雷利还被视为英国帝国主义的象征性人物，他的政策反映了当时英国对全球影响力的追求。总体而言，他被定位为一位具有远见卓识的政治家，其遗产对英国保守主义和现代政治制度产生了深远影响。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Disraeli is regarded as a key figure in Britain's political transition period. He represents the complex process of Britain's shift from aristocratic to democratic politics in the 19th century. Historians generally consider him a pragmatic politician capable of balancing tradition with reform. In popular culture, he is often depicted as an oratorical genius and political strategist, with his rivalry with Gladstone seen as a classic对决 in British political history. His literary works and political writings are also studied as important materials for understanding 19th-century British political thought. Disraeli is also seen as a symbolic figure of British imperialism, with his policies reflecting Britain's pursuit of global influence at the time. Overall, he is positioned as a visionary statesman whose legacy has had a profound impact on British conservatism and modern political institutions.

self.zh: 保守党是民族的有机组成部分，而不仅仅是政治机器。
self.en: The Conservative Party is an organic part of the nation, not merely a political machine.
